candidate.topic: Fasting glucose comparison before October 6 visit
candidate.why_now: The recorded October 6 visit is a decision point, and the available watch data cannot show whether fasting glucose is lower since the breakfast change. There is still time to obtain a relevant comparison.
candidate.what_changed: A September 22 note records an October 6 endocrinology visit to decide next steps. The earlier analysis mentions one fasting glucose value of 108 mg/dL and no later value; no newer glucose measurement was found. The available watch samples are steps and sleep, not glucose.
candidate.unknowns: The original method and date for the 108 mg/dL result are not verified, so a later value cannot yet be assumed comparable. Even a comparable lower result would show a difference at that measurement, not that breakfast caused it or that the change persisted.
candidate.next_step: If the earlier report confirms the method, bring it to the visit and, before then, obtain one fasting glucose result using the same method and unit. A comparable result would help decide whether to discuss a measured decrease or whether more follow-up measurements are needed; it would not establish why the value changed.
